title: Do You Know Why Oil Changes Are Important?
blocks: Oil changes are one of the essential car maintenance items that you should take care of. It is recommended that most vehicles have an oil change every 3,000 miles or every three months, whichever is shorter. As a conscientious driver, you will want to know why oil changes are important. This will help ensure that you will keep oil changes in mind as time goes by and not get distracted by other things.
Why are Oil Changes so significant?

Motor oil helps keep the engine lubricated and prevents excessive friction between the various engine components resulting in premature wear. Some of the oil evaporates in the process and also picks up gunk from the engine. Having regular oil changes removes this debris and keeps the engine from breaking down and extends the life of the investment in your car and prevents engine deterioration.
Know how to save money on Oil Changes?

Ask your auto shop for oil change coupons to reduce the cost. Another way to save is to bundle oil changes with other services like repairs and inspections. Some auto shops will even throw in an oil change for cost if you have major repairs done. Do you know why oil changes are important?

title: Why is Transmission Service Critical For Your Vehicle?
blocks: An important part owning a car is regular maintenance and upkeep. In particular, having a transmission service performed will go a long way in extending the life of your car. While it may seem like a simple process, the transmission is actually one of the most intricate systems in your car. Aside from providing your car with fresh fluid for lubrication and cooling, a lot of build-up will be removed, which if left untreated can result in your car being harder to steer, puddles of fluid left on your driveway, and gears jerking and slipping. Unfortunately, many drivers think regular transmission service isn’t affordable, which can actually lead to more extensive and costly transmission repair.

A transmission repair may seem daunting, but it is typically worth the money spent. Aside from checking to make sure the car is working, a repair will also provide you with an update on the health of your car, as well as with peace of mind! By knowing where problem areas may develop you are able to not only protect yourself, but also better protect your car from having a full transmission replacement.

A full replacement is one of the most costly services for car owners, but by having a routine service, or a necessary repair before little problems become big ones, you not only save money, but you will also help to keep you and your family safer while driving.

title: Anxious About What are the Signs of a Dying Car Battery?
blocks: Have you rushed out the door on your way to work and find that your car won’t start? You wonder if the battery is dead, or if the alternator starting to fail? If you know what are the signs of a dying car battery, you will save yourself frustration and inconvenience by know when to take care of a car battery replacement before you’re left stranded in your driveway.
So do you know what are the signs of a dying car battery? Here are the most common signs that you may start to experience:
Slow engine crank. A car that is hard to start or won’t start at all.
Clicking sound when turning the key. A rapid clicking sound indicates that the available power is too low to crank the engine.
Dim headlights. They aren’t getting enough power.
Electrical problems. The electronic accessories (power seats, power windows, radio, dashboard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, and more) aren’t getting enough power to function properly.

Dashboard warning light. This light (typically in the shape of a car battery) indicates a bad battery, a failing alternator, or some other issue with the electrical system. You have the electrical system inspected by a certified technician.

Swollen battery case. Constant exposure to extreme temperatures (especially repeated freezing and thawing) can cause the sides of the battery case to swell. A car battery replacement will be necessary if this happens.

Old battery. A car battery usually only lasts around four to five years, based on exposure to extreme temperatures and your driving habits. If your battery is getting close to the four-year mark, have it tested frequently.
Loose battery terminals. If you have tightened the terminals and the battery still seems as if it is dying, it is time for a car battery replacement.
A light was left on. If your battery is good and there are none of the problems described above, a simple recharge may be all that is needed to recharge the battery.

title: Schedule a Pre-Trip Inspection at your Auto Repair Shop
blocks: Car problems on a long road trip can be a frustrating experience, not to mention expensive! After one has spent weeks and months planning their summer road trip—where to go and what to see—checking out their vehicle is often overlooked. A pre-trip inspection will make you’re your vehicle has the appropriate auto repair services needed to help avoid breakdowns and find yourself looking for an auto repair shop in a strange town.
Here are some of the auto repair services that should be considered:

Tires—Check tires for the correct air pressure, tread wear, and if there are any bulges and bald spots. Under-inflated tires lower fuel efficiency and increase the risk of damage to your tires. Uneven tread wear indicates that an alignment service may be needed, or you may actually need to invest in new tires before your trip.
Hoses and belts—Hoses and belts can become cracked and brittle as they age. They are vital to the proper functioning of the electrical system, air conditioning, power steering, and cooling system.

Filters and fluids—This includes the motor oil, power steering, brake, and transmission fluids, as well as the antifreeze/coolant mixture in the radiator and the windshield washer solvent in the water reservoir.
Lights—All lights (both interior and exterior) should be working so that you can see and be seen. Have burned-out or broken bulbs replaced at your auto repair shop before leaving on your trip?
Wiper blades—If the blades are more than six months old, they may need to be replaced so you can see clearly when driving during a sudden summer rainstorm.
Brakes—Have the pads and rotors inspected and repaired if necessary to make sure you are not sliding through stop signs.
Battery—Make sure the battery connection is clean, tight and corrosion-free, and that the battery is holding a strong charge.
Tune up—A tune up before your trip will help the engine deliver the best balance of power and fuel economy.

Remember: There is no guarantee that the unexpected flat tire or break-down won’t happen, but you can reduce the chance of unplanned, costly car trouble by taking care of any necessary auto repair services at your favorite auto repair shop before hitting the road.

title: How Often Should You Buy New Tires?
blocks: When Should You Buy New Tires?

Tires are fundamental in keeping your car driving as straight as it should. Good tires also ensure a smoother ride. It’s important to stay on top of tire pressure and make sure it’s right where your vehicle manual says its should be, and to make sure your tires aren’t losing air. But sometimes there are issues when immediate tire repair is needed. There will come a time that your tires need to be replaced. You may be wondering how often should you buy new tires? They can be a hit to your budget!

Once in a while tires will run over a small object that might poke a little hole in them. If you’re close to your car you may hear the air leaking out in a hissing noise. So long as the tire has not gone completely flat yet, you might be able to fix it with a quick patch solution like “Fix-a-flat.” But be warned that substances like that are just simply there to use until you can get your tire patched. Tire repair through patching can do more for a small puncture by making sure it’s completely plugged and usually, the tire can continue to be used if no other internal or external damage has been done. If the tire has been cut, has damage to its interior walls or has been flat for a while, it must be replaced.
How often should you Buy new Tires?

The answer to this question: “how often should you buy new tires”. It also can have a lot to do with the condition of your tires and rubber. Besides simply being damaged by running flat tire or being torn by an object in the road, tire tread can also wear off after a certain amount of miles. You’ll notice the tread is worn by sticking a penny in the tread and seeing how far down it goes. You’ll also notice unusual noises, uneven turning, and shaking and vibrating if your tread is getting worn. Once you’ve noticed any sign of the tread wearing or tires going flat constantly, you should have them replaced immediately. Nowadays, The tires are designed to do 50,000 – 60,000 miles. But when they get down to those tire wear bars, you don’t have as much tread.

title: Engine Service: What It Will Do For Your Vehicle!
blocks: What happens when you are driving down the street and you begin to smell something burning? Do you look around to see if there is an older vehicle or large truck behind you? Do you begin searching your dashboard for warning lights that may be on? Do you immediately think the worst? Of course, a burning smell doesn’t always mean that your car needs a trip to the auto shop for engine repair. However, you would be wise to take your car in to an engine service center for an inspection. That smell could just be some old oil from the last oil change burning off on the engine. Or it could really mean that you need to schedule an engine service as soon as possible for a little work.

If you see smoke coming from under the hood you should stop the car immediately, check the car engine temperature gauge and check the water levels in the radiator and engine. Caution! Do not remove water pump or other caps from under the hood until they cool. The liquids inside are extremely hot and you could receive severe burns. Call an engine repair technician and have them take a look under the hood for you. Because of their experience and training, they will be able to provide you with great engine service and can tell you what the problem is in no time.

Another issue to consider is that water can leak from tiny holes in the water pump and water reserve areas. If not checked on a regular basis, over time the water may all leak out and the engine will begin to run hot. This can cause cracked heads if the pump is not given the right amount of water immediately. Never let the well run dry because it can damage the engine beyond repair.

Changing the oil every 3000 miles will also keep your engine running smooth. Oil changes go hand in hand with changing oil filters, air filters, greasing the engine, and checking the fluid levels. This routine engine service will save you loads of money in engine repair.

title: Are Your Old Tires Done In?
blocks: When it comes to tires, it’s always best to keep up with them by making sure they have enough air and that the tread is not too worn down. One way to tell if you need new tires is the penny method. This can be done by placing a penny head first into the tire tread. If you can see Lincoln’s head, your tread is too low and your tires need to be replaced. Replacing worn tires saves you money and is a safety precaution everyone should take. Worn down tread can result in fewer miles per gallon as well as sliding in wet or icy road conditions.

A couple of tips: Because of road conditions changing during the fall and winter months, you may want to go ahead and change out your tires for a better tread that is meant to handle those specific conditions. Also, it’s highly recommended that you check tire pressure often whether your tires are new or old. If you constantly find that they are significantly low, you may want to have them replace them with new tires.

Many drivers prefer to have their new tires installed by professionals due to the fact that they are done right, it’s easier, and faster. One of the biggest reasons to have them installed professionally is because often times there are guarantees on the miles in the event that the tire does not meet the expected miles. Even though there may be an upfront cost they actually save you money in gas later on.

Tip to remember: When it comes to selecting new tires, consider the upcoming seasons and choose a brand that is known for its quality as well as how many miles you can expect. Even though they may be a little more costly upfront, they actually save you money in fuel and repairs later on.

title: 4 Tips for Quality Auto Repair Services!
blocks: No matter the age of your vehicle, old or new, it’s just a matter of time before you will be looking for auto repair and maintenance services. There seems to be an auto shop on every corner competing for your attention with tempting special deals. How do you know where to go to make sure you receive quality auto repair services?
To receive the best auto repair services possible, here are four things to look for when visiting an auto repair shop:

AAA Approved – If you see that an auto repair shop is a member of the Automobile Association of America (AAA), you know that they have met rigorous industry standards and are qualified to offer a wide variety of services.

ASE Certified – Make sure the auto shop employs ASE-certified technicians. The Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) organization tests the technical skills of mechanics in training who desire to become professionals. These technicians must show their competence in all aspects of auto repair services in order to receive the ASE Certification after taking the required courses and passing tests.
Use of OEM Replacement Parts – Ask if the shop uses OEM (original equipment manufacturer) replacement parts. These are the highest quality parts and are the exact replacement of the original parts.

Special Discount Offers – Auto repair often occurs unexpectedly, so discounts are usually happily accepted by customers. Many auto repair shops will offer rotating special offers and discounts to their regular customers or to first-time new customers.

title: 4 Reasons Why Car Battery Keeps Dying
blocks: When your car battery keeps dying at inconvenient times, it’s frustrating and annoying since most of our vehicle trips are necessary—school, work, groceries, doctor visits, etc. Just in case a driver should forget the importance of car battery maintenance when it can’t do its job, we are reminded of its importance. Take care of your vehicle’s battery and it will take care of you.

The primary function of a car battery is to start the engine by powering the starter motor to provide electric power to the spark plugs in order to ignite the vehicle’s fuel. The car battery also provides power for other components such as lights, horn and climate control system. Batteries do not last the life of a vehicle. After three or four years, it will eventually start to indicate signs of aging and you will find yourself looking for a car battery replacement. However, if your battery is fairly new and it continues to die, there is a serious problem.
Consider the four reasons below why a car battery keeps dying:

Frequent short trips. If you are always making short trips, this may cause your battery to die prematurely. Your vehicle’s ignition is one of the largest users of electrical battery power. If you keep starting and stopping your vehicle without sufficient time for your alternator to recharge the battery, this is one of the reasons why your car battery keeps dying prematurely.

Inoperable charging system. In order for your car battery to recharge, your vehicle’s alternator must provide it with electrical current. If it is not working properly, this is another common reason why your car battery keeps dying.

Extreme Hot and Cold Temperatures. Temperatures that rise above 100 degrees or below 10 degrees Fahrenheit can be very harsh on the life of your car battery. A build-up of lead sulfate crystals can occur when leaving your vehicle in these temperatures for too long. The sulfate buildup can shorten the life of your battery and require more time for it to be recharged.

Poor Battery Maintenance. Failing to have your battery checked and serviced on a regular basis can also cause batteries to wear out too soon. Battery cables, posts, and water levels need to be checked to ensure the battery is producing the required voltage supply to run your vehicle.
